In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, there is complex tear (main horizontal and vertical components) at the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is bone bruise at the posterolateral tibial plateau.  
 The patellofemoral joint appears congruent. There is no cartilage injury. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no tibial translation. 
 There is grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers). There is partial tear of the posteromedial oblique ligament. There is grade II ligamentous sprain of the lateral collateral ligament, at mid substance. Partial tear of the intra-articular portion, popliteus tendon is present. There are tears of the meniscopopliteal fascicles. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. 
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of right knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal.   -- Complex tear (main horizontal and vertical components) at the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.  
 -- Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. 
 -- Grade II ligamentous sprain (partial tear) of the medial collateral ligament, at mid substance (deep and superficial fibers).  
 -- Posterolateral corner injury by evidence of  
 --      Grade II ligamentous sprain of the lateral collateral ligament, at mid substance.

FINDINGS: A partial injury of the anterior cruciate ligament is demonstrated - anatomical continuity is best appreciated in the coronal plane. There is in fact no associated anterior tibial translation.  Well-preserved medial and lateral tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage surfaces, a subcentimeter focus of grade 3/4 articular cartilage loss is noted at the midline femoral trochlea anteriorly. Well-preserved retropatellar articular cartilage.  There is a significant, incompletely imaged knee joint effusion with nonspecific synovitis, no intra-articular loose bodies are present.  There is a popliteus muscle strain posteriorly, there is however no disruption of the corresponding musculotendinous unit or tendon.  The popliteofibular ligament appears sprained, there is furthermore soft tissue edema like signal change at the position of the arcuate ligament complex, suggestive of a sprain pattern - both limbs of the arcuate ligament can however be appreciated on coronal images (series 301 image 26), implying gross structural continuity.  Both collateral ligaments appear intact, as do the PCL, medial meniscus, patellar tendon, distal iliotibial band and marrow signal characteristics.  A tiny cleft is affecting the free edge of the lateral meniscus, at the junction between the body and anterior horn. Minor non calcific distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis also present.
